basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 2.' and it opens '(Cap. XLIV.—Vers. 2.) Et pone argentum uniuscujusque in ore sacculi, et condy meum'. Migne prints the chapter at the head of this block.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XLIV.—Vers. 2.) Et pone argentum uniuscujusque in ore sacculi, et condy meum argenteum mitte in sacculum junioris. Pro sacculo, peronem, vel follem, in Hebraeo habet. Pro condy, id est, poculo, quod etiam in Isaia legimus (LI, 17), Aquila, scyphum, Symmachus phialam transtulerunt.
